projects.tagline: A Lean 4 proof that $p_{n+1} - p_n \leq 246$ for infinitely many $n$.
projects.summary: Formalizes Maynard's multidimensional sieve and the part of Polymath8b that brings the bound to $246$, on top of Mathlib and Kontorovich and Tao's PrimeNumberTheoremAnd. The Lean code is released as PrimeGapsLib.

projects.title: The Classification of Finite Simple Groups, Formalized in Lean

ai.label: AI-assisted
ai.note: The Lean proofs were produced by swarms of AxiomProver agents; the mathematical obstructions they ran into were handled by hand.

projects.tagline: A Lean formalization of the classification of finite simple groups, following the first-generation proof.
projects.summary: Every finite simple group is cyclic of prime order, alternating, of Lie type, or one of the 26 sporadic groups. The original proof runs to some 15,000 journal pages written over several decades; the formalization is about 43 million lines of Lean, produced over 24 days.
description: Formalizing the first-generation argument turned up counterexamples to a closure assertion used in a published route to the Unbalanced Group Theorem. That and the other departures from the literature are recorded in the errata.

outputs.citation: The Unbalanced Group Theorem, Hexagon 2610.00575 (2026), contributed by Colin Defant and Ken Ono.
outputs.scope: The counterexamples, and an alternative argument for the simple-group case using Solomon's theory of maximal 2-components.
